To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed and demonstrated a 0.15 mm 2, 6–18-GHz, 40-W reactively matched GaN MMIC power amplifier with 30 W to 52 W output power and 13 %–30 % power-added-efficiency.
a 6–18-GHz, 40 W, reactively matched GaN MMIC power amplifier with 21.7-dB average small-signal, 30.5-W to 52.7-W output, and 13–30% average power added efficiency was demonstrated.
a 6–18 GHz 40 W GaN MMIC power amplifier has been designed, fabricated, and measured.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation, and measurement of a wideband, reacti-vely matched, 6-18 GHz, 40 W, two-stage, GaN MMIC PA.
the design and performance of GaN-based power amplifiers for wideband applications.
the design of wide-band power amplifiers for applications in the 6–40 GHz frequency range.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design, fabrication, and measurement of the MMIC power amplifier presented in this paper demonstrate a new level of performance for a reactively matched GaN MMIC power amplifier.
a 6–18GHz 40W power amplifier was successfully demonstrated in 0.18μm Scaled-Channel No-Field- Plate GaN process.

this work presents a 40 W reactively matched power MMIC amplifier that covers the 6–17.8 GHz range with a 40.4 W average output power, 13 % to over 30% power-added efficiency, and a 20.8 to 21.7 average gain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a wide-bandwidth power amplifier can be achieved by using a reactively matched design, and that the reactively matched design is not only suitable for wide-bandwidth power amplifiers, but also for wide-bandwidth low-noise amplifiers.
the 40 W GaN MMIC is capable of providing 40 W output power with an average efficiency of 13 %, and 52.8W with 30% efficiency.
a 40 W, 6–18 GaN MMIC PA is now available, which can be used in the next generation of radar and communication systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reactively matched power amplifiers (RMPAs) are capable of achieving high output power with high power added efficiencies (PAEs) at wide bandwidths.
the use of reactively matched output networks can be a very effective means to achieve high output power and high efficiency in a wide bandwidth.

the reactively matched amplifier is able to achieve high output power with good gain over a broad bandwidth, and the reactively matched design can be used to achieve high output-power MMICs with good gain and efficiency over a broad frequency range.
